title: Finite-support assembly from invertible module evaluation
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $U$ an open and $P,F$ cochain complexes of module sheaves on the localized site of $U$. Assume there exist integers $a,b$ such that $P^r$ is a zero object for $r<a$ or $r>b$. Suppose, for every integer $r$ and every module sheaf $B$, the canonical comparison $B\otimes\mathcal Hom(P^r,\mathcal O_U)\to\mathcal Hom(P^r,B)$ is an isomorphism [lem-pc-finite-projective-internal-hom-evaluation defines this comparison]. Put $S=\mathcal O_U[0]$ and $D=\mathcal Hom^\bullet(P,S)$ [def-pur-hom-complex]. If $f:\operatorname{Tot}(F\otimes D)\to\mathcal Hom^\bullet(P,F)$ [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] is a chain map whose component from $F^p\otimes D^q$ in degree $k=p+q$ to $\mathcal Hom(P^r,F^{r+k})$ is zero for $r+q\neq0$ and otherwise is the adjunct of dual evaluation followed by the unit action on $F^p$ [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed], then $f^n$ is an isomorphism for every integer $n$. No bound on $F$, finite-free retract assumption on $P^r$, or affineness of $U$ is assumed.

proof.text: Use homComplex_projections_exists to expose the product projections of the chosen Hom complex without reducing its full bifunctor existence statement. The product projections of Hom(P,S) identify its degree q with Hom(P^(-q),O_U): every other term of S is zero, internal Hom into zero is zero, and a product of one object with zero objects is that object by its universal property. Bounded support of P also makes this dual zero outside [-b,-a].

For fixed n, discard zero terms outside the finite support in the tensor coproduct and Hom product. Reindex by r=-q, p=r+n. The finite product and coproduct agree as a biproduct. The specified component equations make the transported f.f n diagonal, with r-th diagonal map the canonical module evaluation for E=P^r, B=F^(r+n), composed with tensor of the dual projection and the degree-equality transport. The supplied invertibility hypothesis, not a finite-projectivity inference, makes every diagonal map invertible.

Take the finite biproduct of the diagonal inverses and conjugate it by the source and target identifications. Inclusions and projections verify the two inverse equations blockwise; off-diagonal composites vanish and diagonal composites are identities. With empty support both objects are zero and the same equations hold.
